one_month_reasoning: The window ends 2026-11-01 (a Sunday), so the last close is Fri Oct 30. The Q3 2026 report has not been scheduled; it is expected about Nov 3, just after the window (sources 14, 3). In-window events: (1) The first AMI lock-up tranche opens 2026-10-25 (a Sunday), so those shares can trade from Oct 26. Per the supervisor's check of the 8-K Item 3.02 (source 3) it is 25% of 4,741,352 issued shares = ~1.19M (~0.8% of shares outstanding), not 1.3M. THL also holds two underwritten block-trade rights, and a block would likely price 3-5% below market. (2) The AMI financial statements 8-K/A is due around mid-October. (3) Late-October hyperscaler capex prints and AI-semi peer earnings matter most, as the September HBM-driven selloff showed (source 11). (4) The stock is up about 21% in two weeks from the ~$106-111 Sep lows, so pre-earnings positioning and momentum roughly offset the lock-up supply. Net: a near-symmetric lognormal at monthly vol 61%/3.5 = ~17.2%, with the median shaded to ~$133.6 for the small overhang.

The 2027 revenue build is raised to $1.30B, anchored on the $1.2B exit run rate, but kept slightly under the $1.33B consensus because 95% of revenue goes through distributors.

bear.story: An explicit 2024-style destock. In 2024, distributor inventory correction cut revenue ~31% (source 20); distributors are now 95% of sales, so '2027 pretty much booked' turns out to be channel backlog. AI-server capex digests, FPGA revenue falls ~25% from the ~$1.0B exit rate, and AMI grows only modestly. 2027 revenue ~$1.0B, EPS ~$2.0 on operating deleverage and $45M of interest, at ~36x trough-earnings multiple = ~$72.

base.story: 2027 revenue ~$1.30B and EPS ~$2.96-3.21, with 2028E ~$3.55-3.85. The multiple compresses from ~44x 2027E to ~38-40x forward, so earnings growth slightly outruns de-rating.

bull.story: AI-server attach and AMI cross-sell keep growth at 35%+. 2028E EPS of $4.5+ holds a mid-40s multiple, above the $180 top target.

thesis_break_reason: $90 is ~30x corrected 2027E EPS of ~$3.0 and ~17-20% below the Aug-Sep 2026 lows ($104-111). Trading there most likely means a Q3/Q4 guide-down showing that the 'booked' 2027 was distributor stocking, an AI-server capex digestion, or AMI customer attrition after it left a chip vendor, rather than ordinary ~60% vol. Leverage would also rise toward 2x+ net debt/EBITDA against covenant tests.

reasoning: Round 2. I accept the supervisor's checked corrections. Consensus 2027 EPS is $3.21 on $1.33B. Management guided a $1.2B exit run rate on the Q2 call. My round-1 2027 revenue haircut to $1.26B was not tied to evidence, and the 54-69x / 511x multiples were screen artefacts; the real figure is ~44x 2027E. So I rebuild 2027 at $1.30B revenue and $2.96 EPS (6% tax, 146M shares, $45M interest), and put the downside into an explicit destock scenario instead of the base. I disagree on one point: the supervisor calls the BofA Sell stale, but StockAnalysis shows BofA kept its Sell on 2026-08-05, after Q2. That is weak evidence, but it means the valuation critique is current and is the only Sell among 13 analysts. Zacks also cut to Hold on 2026-09-08. My skeptic research again found no short report, litigation or accounting red flag, and insider selling is small and routine. The bear case remains valuation, channel concentration and leverage. Fair value rises from $125 to $131 (P/E $135, EV/EBITDA $125), still just under spot. The ladder is a mixture of 78% lognormal with median $148 and sigma 0.45 (base+bull) and 22% bear lognormal with median $75 and sigma 0.36, anchored on the 2024 ~31% revenue drop. The bear median is unchanged, and the base median rises from $145 to $148 on the corrected EPS. That gives mean ~$145, P(>=134) = 0.47 (from 0.455) and P(<94) ~ 28%. I keep the left tail fatter than the supervisor's because 95% distributor mix plus 88% receivable concentration is exactly what turned 2024 into a ~31% revenue decline. Research was limited to 2 extra queries.
